question: how much of the +13.8pp empty-answer artifact does the fixed answerer actually recover?
design: identical protocol to lme2-web-medium-full (240 questions, web union-store, deterministic specs + glm-5.3 llm judges, CPU) with the two-stage fixed answerer: max_tokens 8192 (thinking completes; worst measured case 5805), fallback retry with thinking disabled on empty text; judge runs thinking-disabled. The artifacted run's 33 empty answers were silently scored wrong.

results.recovered: +5.4pp (13 of the 33 recovered answers scored correct; 39% of recoveries were right)

findings: The measurement artifact is fully eliminated (0 empty answers) and the honest web-medium text-arm number is 0.250, not 0.1958.

Recovery is +5.4pp of the +13.8pp ceiling: 20 of the 33 previously-empty answers were answered but scored wrong - the empty answers were concentrated on reasoning-heavy questions where the model, given the budget, still does not answer correctly. The artifact inflated the apparent gap; the real gap is capability, not budget.
Latency unchanged (p50 2.5s): the 8192 budget costs nothing when thinking finishes early.
honest_reading: single re-run, no variance repetition (judge temperature 0; SC absent in this runner so variance is minimal); enterprise-medium keeps its 0.1943 artifacted number (5.7pp ceiling; a re-run costs a 14h reseed for ~12 questions - uneconomical, disclosed here); LAFS recomputed with the fixed web point - medium gain remains exactly 0.0 (25.0 < 45.9 floor).
